subject: EdgeWorks — connectivity approach for Redwood Private (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@edgeworks.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeWorks NetOps <netops@edgeworks.com>
Date: 2025-07-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Connectivity options for Redwood Private deployment

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. EdgeWorks is excited to move forward with a Private deployment of Redwood in our us-east-1 account. Before we get the PO out, the network team needs your recommendation on the connection pattern. Our priorities are:
- sub-10ms p99 latency for request/response in-region
- predictable throughput (2000 req/s typical, bursts to 8k)
- strong security controls and auditability
- support for cross-account team boundaries (our app and infra live in different AWS accounts)

Can you outline pros/cons between VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and a site-to-site VPN to your on-prem staging environment? Also any operational prerequisites we should plan for (routing, proxy, NAT, peering limits).

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30m tech sync with our netops next week.

Appreciate it —
Sarah
Director, Platform Engineering, EdgeWorks

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@edgeworks.com>
Cc: EdgeWorks NetOps <netops@edgeworks.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-07-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Connectivity options for Redwood Private deployment

Thanks Sarah — good questions. Below is a concise comparison plus our recommended pilot path. I attached a short matrix and a draft test plan.

Summary (short):
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints) + regional endpoint in your account: best combination of security isolation, cross-account access, and operational traceability. Keeps traffic on AWS backbone and gives you per-ENI access control.
- VPC Peering: lowest operational latency in same-region, but does NOT support transitive routing across accounts/peers. If you need to connect multiple EdgeWorks accounts or share with a partner VPC hub, peering becomes hard to scale and requires explicit route management.
- Site-to-site VPN: encrypted but variable latency and throughput. Good as fallback or for non-latency-critical access; introduces an extra network hop and more ops surface.

Tradeoffs / details:
- Latency: Peering typically lowest (no endpoint), PrivateLink adds ~1–3ms of overhead at p50/p95 for us-east; VPN adds jitter and larger p99. For your sub-10ms p99 target, PrivateLink in-region should be fine if RTT to our regional endpoint is <7–8ms (we can validate).
- Throughput: PrivateLink scales with ENIs and endpoint bandwidth limits; design for multiple ENIs per AZ. Peering has no per-connection ENI limits but is limited by instance/network throughput. VPN is most constrained unless you choose Transit Gateway + HA VPN or Direct Connect.
- Cross-account: PrivateLink is explicitly cross-account-friendly (you create a service, you accept endpoint connections). Peering requires peering relationships in each account pair (operationally painful for many accounts).
- Security & Audit: PrivateLink keeps a clear service boundary — we can emit per-ENI flow logs and tie requests to endpoint connections. Peering exposes route tables across accounts (more blast radius). VPN gives you encrypted WAN but less integration with IAM-based controls.
- Routing complexity: Peering requires routes and careful avoidance of overlapping CIDRs; PrivateLink avoids transitive routing concerns.
- Cost: PrivateLink incurs hourly ENI/endpoint charges + data processing per GB. Peering has data transfer costs in some clouds and no hourly charge. VPN has obviously lower infra cost but higher egress and operational engineering.

Recommended pilot:
1) Create a Redwood Private service endpoint in our tenant (us-east-1).
2) EdgeWorks provisions an Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) in your primary app account and AZs (start with 2 AZs).
3) Run perf tests (attached test plan): p50/p95/p99 latency, sustained throughput 2k req/s for 30m, burst tests to 8k, error rate, and auth path validation.
4) If you need sub-5ms p99, consider intra-VPC peering for same-account flows or a co-located peering relationship in a shared-ops account, but note scaling limits.

Operational prerequisites:
- Non-overlapping CIDR between your endpoint subnet and our service network.
- Security group rules on the interface endpoint allowing Redwood service ENIs and port ranges we define (443/TCP + health-check ports).
- IAM policy or endpoint service acceptance configured for cross-account connect.
- Flow logs enabled for the endpoint subnets for audit and perf baseline.
- Optional: Route53 private hosted zone delegation if you want DNS-based routing to the endpoint.

Next steps: I can run the pilot once you confirm we should proceed. Also propose a 30m tech sync Thursday 7/10 at 10am ET to align with NetOps.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

+1 on PrivateLink for the first pass. Quick notes to add for procurement and quota planning:
- PrivateLink endpoints = hourly + data processing — include allowance in recurring costs (we usually model 0.5–1.5TB/mo for typical usage).
- ENI/quota: ask EdgeWorks to check EC2 ENI quotas per AZ and increase ahead of time if they plan >4 endpoints.
- Cross-account onboarding: we have a short onboarding playbook (I can share) that reduces acceptance friction.

I can also help field pricing questions with legal/procurement once the pilot bill-of-materials is clearer.

—Ben
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Thanks Kimberly & Ben — this is helpful and aligns with what our netops expected. We are happy to pilot PrivateLink in us-east-1. Action items from our side:
- NetOps will open a Service Quota request for EC2 ENIs in us-east-1 (target 50 ENIs across AZs).
- We'll provision two endpoint subnets (one per AZ) and enable flow logs; diagram attached.
- Please share the onboarding playbook and the expected endpoint security group/IP ranges you will ask us to allow.

Let's lock the tech sync for Thu 2025-07-10 10:00 ET. Sarah and our lead network engineer (cc'd) will join.

FYI: We still want a fallback path — please include a short runbook for traffic degrade to an HA VPN if the PrivateLink region has an incident.

Appreciate the clear recommendation.

—Sarah
